metadata.description: Reference cards for ICU Clinical Grouping Evidence Agent System
metadata.model: LSTM predicting top-5 of 21 clinical groupings from 12hr ICU vitals
metadata.usage: Each Evidence Agent receives one card + patient data summary to generate clinical reasoning justification

HEART_FAILURE.definition: Inability of the heart to pump sufficient blood to meet metabolic demands. HFrEF (EF≤40%), HFmrEF (EF 41-49%), HFpEF (EF≥50%). Acute decompensation triggered by ischemia, arrhythmia, infection, dietary indiscretion, medication non-adherence.

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia (compensatory); may be bradycardic if on beta-blockers or with conduction disease
vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Can be hypertensive (flash pulmonary edema) or hypotensive (cardiogenic shock); narrow pulse pressure suggests low output
vital_sign_patterns.respiratory_rate: Elevated (>20) from pulmonary congestion; Cheyne-Stokes pattern possible
vital_sign_patterns.spo2: Reduced due to pulmonary edema; may require high FiO2 or NIV
vital_sign_patterns.characteristic_pattern: Tachycardia + tachypnea + hypoxemia + elevated JVP + peripheral edema

key_labs.bnp_ntprobnp: BNP >100 pg/mL or NT-proBNP >300 pg/mL supports diagnosis; higher levels = worse prognosis
key_labs.troponin: May be elevated from demand ischemia or acute coronary syndrome trigger
key_labs.creatinine: Cardiorenal syndrome common; rising Cr limits diuretic efficacy
key_labs.sodium: Hyponatremia (<135) indicates neurohormonal activation and worse prognosis
key_labs.lactate: Elevated in cardiogenic shock indicating tissue hypoperfusion

stages.A: At risk, no structural disease or symptoms
stages.C: Structural disease with current or prior symptoms

nyha_class.III: Marked limitation, comfortable only at rest

key_differentiators.vs_PNEUMONIA: Both cause dyspnea/hypoxia; HF has elevated BNP, bilateral edema, response to diuretics; pneumonia has fever, focal consolidation, elevated procalcitonin
key_differentiators.vs_COPD_ASTHMA: Both cause dyspnea; HF has elevated BNP, bilateral crackles, peripheral edema; COPD has wheezing, hyperinflation, response to bronchodilators
key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_MI: MI can cause acute HF; check troponin trend, ECG for ischemic changes

sources: Heidenreich PA et al. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure. Circulation 2022;145:e895-e1032
McDonagh TA et al. 2021 ESC Guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic HF. Eur Heart J 2021;42:3599-3726

SEPSIS.definition: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by dysregulated host response to infection. Septic shock = sepsis + vasopressor requirement + lactate >2 despite adequate fluid resuscitation.

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia (>90-100 bpm) - early and sensitive sign
vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Hypotension (MAP <65 or SBP <90); may be normal early then decompensate
vital_sign_patterns.temperature: Fever (>38.3°C) OR hypothermia (<36°C) - hypothermia worse prognosis
vital_sign_patterns.spo2: Variable; may need supplemental O2 for target >94%
vital_sign_patterns.characteristic_pattern: Early (warm shock): tachycardia, warm extremities, wide pulse pressure, bounding pulses. Late (cold shock): hypotension, cool mottled extremities, narrow pulse pressure

key_labs.lactate: ≥2 mmol/L indicates tissue hypoperfusion; >4 = severe; serial trending important
key_labs.procalcitonin: Elevated supports bacterial infection; helps guide antibiotic duration
key_labs.bilirubin: Elevated indicates hepatic dysfunction (hepatic SOFA component)

diagnostic_criteria.septic_shock: Sepsis + vasopressor to maintain MAP ≥65 + lactate >2 despite adequate fluids
diagnostic_criteria.qsofa: ≥2 of: RR ≥22, altered mentation, SBP ≤100 (screening, not diagnostic)
diagnostic_criteria.hour_1_bundle: Measure lactate, obtain cultures, administer broad-spectrum antibiotics, begin fluids (30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension or lactate ≥4), vasopressors if hypotensive during/after fluids

key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: Both cause hypotension and tachycardia; sepsis has infection source, elevated lactate/procalcitonin, warm shock early; HF has elevated BNP, pulmonary edema, cold extremities
key_differentiators.vs_TOXIC_METABOLIC: AWS has tremor, responds to BZD; DKA has hyperglycemia, ketones, anion gap; both can have SIRS-like picture
key_differentiators.vs_PANCREATITIS: Severe pancreatitis mimics sepsis; lipase elevated; infected necrosis = true sepsis

sources: Evans L et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines 2021. Intensive Care Med 2021;47:1181-1247
Singer M et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315:801-810

TOXIC_METABOLIC.definition: Metabolic derangements requiring ICU care including alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS), diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS), and electrolyte emergencies.

aws.characteristic: Tremor, agitation, hallucinations; delirium tremens 48-96h after last drink

dka_hhs.respiratory_rate: Kussmaul breathing (deep, rapid) in DKA from metabolic acidosis
dka_hhs.temperature: May be hypothermic; fever suggests infection trigger

aws.ast_alt: AST:ALT ratio >2:1 suggests alcoholic liver disease
aws.blood_alcohol: May be zero at time of withdrawal

dka.potassium: Total body depleted despite initial normal/high levels

diagnostic_criteria.ciwa_ar: Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol (does NOT include vital signs): <8 mild, 8-15 moderate, ≥16 severe. Invalid in delirium tremens - use CAM-ICU/RASS

red_flags: Delirium tremens (3-5% of hospitalized AWS; mortality 5-15% untreated)
DKA: pH <7.0, K+ <3.3 before insulin, cerebral edema

key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: AWS has tremor, responds to BZD; sepsis has infection source, elevated procalcitonin
key_differentiators.vs_LIVER_FAILURE: AWS has sympathetic hyperactivity; hepatic encephalopathy has elevated ammonia, asterixis, responds to lactulose
key_differentiators.vs_STROKE_NEURO: AWS seizures are generalized; focal deficits suggest structural cause

sources: ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management. J Addiction Med 2020
Kitabchi AE et al. Hyperglycemic Crises in Adult Patients With Diabetes. Diabetes Care 2009;32:1335-43

CORONARY_ARTERY_DZ.definition: Chronic coronary artery disease with stable angina or prior MI, without acute plaque rupture. Distinguished from ACUTE_MI by absence of acute troponin rise/fall pattern.

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: May be normal or controlled with beta-blockers; tachycardia suggests decompensation
vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Often hypertensive; target BP control to reduce oxygen demand
vital_sign_patterns.characteristic: Stable pattern without acute hemodynamic changes; exertional symptoms

key_labs.troponin: Normal or chronically mildly elevated (type 2 MI pattern) - NO acute rise/fall
key_labs.bnp: May be elevated if concurrent HF
key_labs.lipids: Often abnormal; target LDL <70 for secondary prevention
key_labs.creatinine: Baseline renal function for medication dosing and contrast use

diagnostic_criteria.diagnosis: Known CAD from prior angiography, prior MI, or prior revascularization
diagnostic_criteria.stable_angina: Predictable exertional symptoms relieved by rest or nitroglycerin

red_flags: Change in anginal pattern (unstable angina → ACUTE_MI)
New troponin elevation with rise/fall (acute coronary syndrome)

key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_MI: CAD is chronic/stable; ACUTE_MI has acute troponin rise/fall, dynamic ECG changes, unstable symptoms
key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: CAD may cause ischemic cardiomyopathy → HF; look for acute decompensation triggers

sources: Virani SS et al. 2023 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease. Circulation 2023
Knuuti J et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for Chronic Coronary Syndromes. Eur Heart J 2020;41:407-477

ACUTE_MI.definition: Acute myocardial infarction from coronary plaque rupture causing acute myocardial ischemia and necrosis. STEMI (ST elevation) or NSTEMI (no ST elevation). Type 1 MI (plaque rupture) vs Type 2 MI (demand ischemia).

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia (pain, sympathetic activation) OR bradycardia (inferior MI, vagal)
vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Hypertension (pain, catecholamines) OR hypotension (cardiogenic shock, RV infarct)
vital_sign_patterns.respiratory_rate: Elevated if pulmonary edema or pain
vital_sign_patterns.spo2: May be reduced with pulmonary edema
vital_sign_patterns.characteristic_pattern: Hemodynamic instability suggests large infarct or mechanical complication

key_labs.troponin: GOLD STANDARD - acute rise and/or fall pattern; high-sensitivity troponin detects smaller MIs earlier
key_labs.bnp: Elevated indicates LV dysfunction; prognostic value
key_labs.cbc: Anemia worsens ischemia; thrombocytopenia affects antiplatelet choice

diagnostic_criteria.guideline: Fourth Universal Definition of MI (2018) / ACC/AHA 2025
diagnostic_criteria.type_2_mi: Oxygen supply/demand mismatch without plaque rupture
diagnostic_criteria.stemi: ST elevation ≥1mm in 2 contiguous leads (≥2mm in V2-V3); emergent reperfusion
diagnostic_criteria.nstemi: Troponin rise/fall + ischemic symptoms/ECG changes; risk stratify for timing of angiography

red_flags: Mechanical complications (VSD, papillary muscle rupture, free wall rupture)
Anterior MI with extensive ST elevation

key_differentiators.vs_CORONARY_ARTERY_DZ: Acute MI has acute troponin rise/fall; CAD has stable or chronically elevated troponin
key_differentiators.vs_PULMONARY_EMBOLISM: Both cause chest pain, dyspnea, troponin elevation; PE has RV strain pattern, hypoxemia, D-dimer; MI has coronary distribution ECG changes
key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: MI can cause acute HF; look for new regional wall motion abnormality, troponin kinetics

sources: Thygesen K et al. Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction. Circulation 2018;138:e618-e651
Rao SV et al. 2025 ACC/AHA Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes. Circulation 2025

AFIB_ARRHYTHMIA.definition: Cardiac arrhythmias requiring ICU management including atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (RVR), atrial flutter, supraventricular tachycardia, ventricular tachycardia, and bradyarrhythmias.

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachyarrhythmia: HR 110-180+ (AF with RVR); Bradyarrhythmia: HR <50 or pauses
vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: May be hypotensive if hemodynamically unstable
vital_sign_patterns.rhythm: AF: irregularly irregular; VT: wide complex regular; SVT: narrow complex regular

key_labs.potassium: Hypokalemia predisposes to arrhythmias; keep K+ >4.0
key_labs.magnesium: Hypomagnesemia predisposes to arrhythmias; keep Mg >2.0
key_labs.troponin: May be elevated from demand ischemia during tachyarrhythmia
key_labs.digoxin_level: If on digoxin, check for toxicity

af_classification.permanent: Accepted, no further rhythm control attempts

diagnostic_criteria.rate_control_target: Lenient (<110 at rest) vs strict (<80) based on symptoms

red_flags: Complete heart block with inadequate escape
WPW with AF (wide irregular - avoid AV nodal blockers)

key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: Sepsis can cause tachycardia and new AF; treat underlying infection
key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_MI: MI can trigger arrhythmias; arrhythmia can cause demand ischemia; check troponin trend
key_differentiators.vs_PULMONARY_EMBOLISM: PE can cause tachycardia, new AF, RV strain; consider if unexplained

sources: Joglar JA et al. 2023 ACC/AHA/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of AF. Circulation 2024;149:e1-e156
Kanji S et al. Treatment of New-Onset AF in Noncardiac ICU Patients. Crit Care Med 2008;36:1620-1624

PNEUMONIA.definition: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma. Community-acquired (CAP), hospital-acquired (HAP), ventilator-associated (VAP), or aspiration pneumonia. ICU admission for severe CAP or respiratory failure.

vital_sign_patterns.respiratory_rate: Tachypnea (≥30/min) - most sensitive vital sign; part of severe CAP criteria
vital_sign_patterns.temperature: Fever (>38°C) typical; elderly may be afebrile
vital_sign_patterns.spo2: Hypoxemia; PaO2/FiO2 ≤250 is severe CAP criterion

key_labs.procalcitonin: Elevated in bacterial pneumonia; helps distinguish from viral; guides antibiotic duration
key_labs.bun: Elevated BUN is part of CURB-65

diagnostic_criteria.severe_cap_definition: 1 major OR ≥3 minor criteria → ICU admission
diagnostic_criteria.curb65: Confusion, Urea >7mmol/L (BUN>19), RR≥30, BP<90/60, Age≥65. Score 3-5 = severe.

key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: Both cause dyspnea, hypoxia; pneumonia has fever, focal consolidation, elevated procalcitonin; HF has elevated BNP, bilateral edema, response to diuretics
key_differentiators.vs_COPD_ASTHMA: Pneumonia can trigger COPD exacerbation; look for focal infiltrate, fever, purulent sputum
key_differentiators.vs_COVID: Similar presentation; test for SARS-CoV-2; COVID has bilateral GGO, lymphopenia, distinct clinical course

sources: Metlay JP et al. Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with CAP: ATS/IDSA 2019. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;200:e45-e67
Lim WS et al. Defining CAP severity on presentation: CURB-65. Thorax 2003;58:377-382

ACUTE_KIDNEY_INJURY.definition: Acute decline in kidney function. Prerenal (hypoperfusion), intrinsic (ATN, AIN, GN), or postrenal (obstruction). KDIGO staging by creatinine rise or urine output decline.

vital_sign_patterns.urine_output: DEFINING parameter - oliguria <0.5 mL/kg/hr for ≥6 hours
vital_sign_patterns.respiratory_rate: Tachypnea if uremic acidosis or volume overload
vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia from hypovolemia; bradycardia if severe hyperkalemia

key_labs.creatinine: Rising trend is diagnostic; rate of rise important
key_labs.potassium: Hyperkalemia - life-threatening; check ECG for peaked T waves, QRS widening
key_labs.urinalysis: Muddy brown casts = ATN; WBC casts = AIN; RBC casts = GN; bland = prerenal

diagnostic_criteria.stage_1: Cr 1.5-1.9x baseline OR +0.3 mg/dL; UO <0.5 mL/kg/hr for 6-12h
diagnostic_criteria.stage_3: Cr ≥3.0x baseline OR ≥4.0 mg/dL OR RRT initiation; UO <0.3 mL/kg/hr for ≥24h OR anuria ≥12h
diagnostic_criteria.rrt_indications: Refractory K+ >6.5, pH <7.1, volume overload, uremic complications, dialyzable toxins

key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: AKI is SOFA renal component in sepsis; sepsis-associated AKI common
key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: Cardiorenal syndrome - HF causes AKI; requires careful volume management
key_differentiators.vs_LIVER_FAILURE: Hepatorenal syndrome - functional AKI in cirrhosis; requires albumin + vasoconstrictors

sources: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for AKI. Kidney Int Suppl 2012;2:1-138
Mortality HR 2.2/6.1/8.6 for KDIGO Stages 1/2/3 respectively

STROKE_NEURO.definition: Acute cerebrovascular event. Ischemic stroke (87%): arterial occlusion. Hemorrhagic stroke (13%): ICH or SAH. ICU for large territory, hemorrhagic conversion, elevated ICP, or intervention.

vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: ELEVATED - permissive hypertension (impaired autoregulation); target <220/120 if no reperfusion; <180/105 post-tPA/thrombectomy
vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: May show AF (embolic source); Cushing reflex (bradycardia + HTN) with herniation
vital_sign_patterns.respiratory: Irregular patterns (Cheyne-Stokes, ataxic) with brainstem involvement

key_labs.glucose: MUST check before tPA - hypoglycemia mimics stroke; hyperglycemia worsens outcomes

diagnostic_criteria.nihss: 0 no symptoms; 1-4 minor; 5-15 moderate; 16-20 moderate-severe; 21-42 severe
diagnostic_criteria.tpa_window: Within 4.5 hours; extended to 9 hours with favorable imaging
diagnostic_criteria.thrombectomy_window: Up to 24 hours for LVO with favorable imaging; strongly recommended for basilar with NIHSS ≥10
diagnostic_criteria.bp_post_reperfusion: Target <180/105 for 24 hours; intensive <140 NOT recommended

red_flags: Malignant MCA syndrome (decompressive craniectomy may be needed)

key_differentiators.vs_SYNCOPE: Stroke has persistent focal deficits; syncope has complete recovery; always do neuro exam
key_differentiators.vs_TOXIC_METABOLIC: Hypoglycemia mimics stroke - ALWAYS check glucose; metabolic causes typically symmetric
key_differentiators.vs_TRAUMA_NEURO: Traumatic vs spontaneous hemorrhage - mechanism critical

sources: Prabhakaran S et al. 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for Early Management of AIS. Stroke 2026
NIH Stroke Scale - standardized assessment

UTI_INFECTION.definition: Urinary tract infection ranging from cystitis to pyelonephritis to urosepsis. ICU admission for urosepsis or complicated UTI with hemodynamic instability.

vital_sign_patterns.temperature: Fever common with pyelonephritis/urosepsis; may be absent in elderly

key_labs.urinalysis: Pyuria (>10 WBC/hpf), bacteriuria, positive nitrites/leukocyte esterase
key_labs.creatinine: May be elevated from obstruction or sepsis-associated AKI

diagnostic_criteria.complicated_uti: UTI in presence of structural/functional abnormality, catheter, obstruction, male sex, pregnancy, or immunocompromise

red_flags: Failure to improve on appropriate antibiotics

key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: Urosepsis is sepsis from urinary source; identify and treat obstruction
key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_KIDNEY_INJURY: UTI can cause AKI; obstructive uropathy needs decompression

sources: IDSA 2025 Guidelines on Complicated UTI
EAU Guidelines on Urological Infections 2024

LIVER_FAILURE.definition: Acute liver failure (ALF): INR ≥1.5 + encephalopathy, no prior liver disease, <26 weeks. Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF): decompensation of cirrhosis. Causes include acetaminophen, viral hepatitis, autoimmune, drug-induced.

vital_sign_patterns.respiratory: Tachypnea/hyperventilation early; intubation for grade 3-4 HE
vital_sign_patterns.mental_status: Altered - DEFINING for ALF; West Haven grading

key_labs.inr: ≥1.5 required for ALF diagnosis; does NOT correlate with bleeding risk in liver disease
key_labs.glucose: Hypoglycemia common (impaired gluconeogenesis); requires continuous monitoring
key_labs.lactate: Elevated; pH <7.3 in acetaminophen = 95% mortality without transplant
key_labs.phosphate: Paradoxically LOW in acetaminophen (indicates regeneration - good sign)

kings_college_criteria.acetaminophen: pH <7.3 OR all 3: INR >6.5, Cr >3.4, grade 3-4 HE
kings_college_criteria.non_acetaminophen: INR >6.5 OR any 3 of 5: unfavorable etiology, age <10 or >40, jaundice >7 days before HE, INR >3.5, bilirubin >17.5

red_flags: Meeting King's College Criteria (list for transplant)

key_differentiators.vs_TOXIC_METABOLIC: HE has elevated ammonia, asterixis, responds to lactulose; AWS has tremor, sympathetic hyperactivity, responds to BZD
key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: Both cause vasodilatory shock; ALF patients at high infection risk
key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_KIDNEY_INJURY: Hepatorenal syndrome = functional AKI; requires albumin + terlipressin

sources: Lee WM et al. AASLD Position Paper: Acute Liver Failure. Hepatology 2011
Flamm SL et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of ALF. Am J Gastroenterol 2023

SURGICAL_COMPLICATION.definition: Complications from surgical procedures requiring ICU: surgical site infection (SSI), anastomotic leak, postoperative bleeding, respiratory failure, sepsis, device complications.

vital_sign_patterns.baseline_context: Abnormal vitals COMMON postop - tachycardia/tachypnea in >50% of uncomplicated recoveries
warning_signs: Failure to progress along expected trajectory
vital_sign_patterns.anastomotic_leak: Typically POD 3-7; early: persistent tachycardia, low-grade fever; late: peritonitis, septic shock
vital_sign_patterns.ppv_note: Single abnormal vital sign has PPV only 4-11% for complications

key_labs.wbc: Leukocytosis expected postop; persistent elevation or rising trend concerning
key_labs.crp: Normally peaks POD 2-3 then declines; failure to decline suggests infection/leak

ssi_cdc.organ_space: Body part opened/manipulated during surgery (includes anastomotic leak)

anastomotic_leak_grading.grade_a: Radiologic leak, no symptoms, no management change
anastomotic_leak_grading.grade_b: Requires intervention (antibiotics, drainage) but no re-operation

diagnostic_criteria.postop_sepsis: Sepsis-3 criteria in postoperative context; consider failure of source control

red_flags: Cardiopulmonary collapse of unclear etiology (suspect anastomotic leak)
Failure to improve despite antibiotics (failure of source control)

key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: Same criteria, but surgical source requires source control consideration
key_differentiators.vs_PNEUMONIA: Postop pneumonia common; distinguish from intra-abdominal source
key_differentiators.vs_PULMONARY_EMBOLISM: PE risk high postop; unexplained hypoxemia/tachycardia → consider CTPA

sources: Barie PS et al. Sepsis and Postoperative SSI. Surgical Clinics 2023
Erb L et al. Abnormal Vital Signs After Bowel Resection. J Am Coll Surg 2014

TRAUMA_NEURO.definition: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) from external mechanical force. Mild (GCS 13-15), Moderate (GCS 9-12), Severe (GCS 3-8). ICU for moderate-severe TBI, ICP monitoring, neurosurgical intervention.

vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Hypotension (SBP <90) DOUBLES MORTALITY - maintain SBP ≥100 (age 50-69) or ≥110 (age 15-49)
vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia common; bradycardia with HTN = Cushing reflex (herniation)
vital_sign_patterns.respiratory: Irregular patterns suggest brainstem injury; intubate for GCS ≤8
vital_sign_patterns.icp: Normal <20 mmHg; treat >22 mmHg per BTF

key_labs.coagulation: TBI causes coagulopathy (tissue factor release); correct urgently
key_labs.glucose: Avoid hypoglycemia; hyperglycemia associated with worse outcomes
key_labs.sodium: Target normal; monitor if using hypertonic saline
key_labs.osmolality: Monitor if using mannitol (limit 320) or hypertonic saline

gcs.eye: Spontaneous (4), To voice (3), To pain (2), None (1)
gcs.motor: Obeys (6), Localizes (5), Withdraws (4), Flexion (3), Extension (2), None (1)

diagnostic_criteria.btf_icp_monitoring: GCS ≤8 with abnormal CT; or normal CT with ≥2 of: age >40, motor posturing, SBP <90

key_differentiators.vs_STROKE_NEURO: Mechanism distinguishes traumatic vs spontaneous; trauma may cause stroke (dissection)
key_differentiators.vs_TOXIC_METABOLIC: Alcohol intoxication complicates GCS; low threshold for imaging
key_differentiators.vs_SYNCOPE: Syncope causes fall → secondary TBI; evaluate both

sources: Carney N et al. BTF Guidelines for Severe TBI, 4th Edition. Neurosurgery 2017;80:6-15
Hawryluk GWJ et al. SIBICC ICP Management Algorithm. Intensive Care Med 2019

GI_BLEED.definition: Upper GI bleed (UGIB): proximal to ligament of Treitz (esophagus, stomach, duodenum). Lower GI bleed (LGIB): distal. Causes: peptic ulcer, varices, Mallory-Weiss, diverticulosis, angiodysplasia.

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia early sign; may be absent with beta-blockers
vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Orthostatic hypotension early; supine hypotension with >30-40% blood loss

key_labs.hemoglobin: May be normal initially (hemodilution takes hours); trend is key
key_labs.coagulation: INR, PTT; correct if >2.5 with active bleeding

glasgow_blatchford_score.components: BUN, Hgb, SBP, HR, melena, syncope, hepatic disease, heart failure
glasgow_blatchford_score.interpretation: Score 0-1: low risk, candidate for outpatient management (100% NPV)

rockall_score.interpretation: ≤2: low risk (4.3% rebleed, 0.1% death); ≥6: high risk (15% rebleed, 39% death)

diagnostic_criteria.aims65: Albumin <3, INR >1.5, Mental status change, SBP ≤90, Age ≥65

red_flags: Active hematemesis or bright red blood per NGT

key_differentiators.vs_LIVER_FAILURE: Variceal bleeding in cirrhosis; coagulopathy; specific treatment (octreotide, TIPS)
key_differentiators.vs_SYNCOPE: GI bleed can present with syncope; check hemoglobin
key_differentiators.vs_SURGICAL_COMPLICATION: Postop bleeding from anastomosis; may need return to OR

sources: Blatchford O et al. GBS validation. Lancet 2000;356:1318-21
Villanueva C et al. Restrictive transfusion strategy in UGIB. NEJM 2013

SKIN_SOFT_TISSUE.definition: Skin and soft tissue infections ranging from cellulitis to necrotizing fasciitis. ICU admission for necrotizing infection, sepsis, or extensive involvement requiring surgical debridement.

vital_sign_patterns.temperature: Fever common; may be absent in immunocompromised
vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia, especially with sepsis or necrotizing infection
vital_sign_patterns.characteristic: Pain out of proportion to exam = red flag for necrotizing fasciitis

key_labs.wbc: Leukocytosis; WBC >15.4k part of LRINEC score

lrinec_score.components: CRP, WBC, Hgb, Na, Creatinine, Glucose
lrinec_score.interpretation: ≥8 = high risk for necrotizing fasciitis; BUT low sensitivity (~60%)
lrinec_score.note: Clinical diagnosis is paramount - do NOT rely solely on LRINEC

necrotizing_fasciitis_clues: Pain out of proportion to exam
Systemic toxicity disproportionate to local findings

red_flags: Pain out of proportion to exam (necrotizing fasciitis)

key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: SSTI can be source of sepsis; identify and control source
key_differentiators.vs_SURGICAL_COMPLICATION: Postop wound infection; may need operative debridement

sources: Stevens DL et al. IDSA Guidelines for SSTI. Clin Infect Dis 2014;59:e10-52
Wong CH et al. LRINEC Score. Crit Care Med 2004;32:1535-41

VALVE_DISEASE.definition: Significant valvular heart disease requiring ICU care. Includes severe aortic stenosis (AS), aortic regurgitation (AR), mitral stenosis (MS), mitral regurgitation (MR). ICU for decompensation, cardiogenic shock, or peri-procedural.

vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: AS: narrow pulse pressure, pulsus parvus et tardus. AR: wide pulse pressure, low diastolic. MR: may be hypotensive in acute severe MR
vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia with decompensation; AF common with mitral disease
vital_sign_patterns.characteristic: Murmur characteristics help identify valve lesion

key_labs.troponin: May be elevated from demand ischemia

diagnostic_criteria.severe_as: AVA <1.0 cm², mean gradient >40 mmHg, peak velocity >4 m/s

red_flags: Severe AS with hypotension (careful with vasodilators)
Acute severe MR or AR (flash pulmonary edema)

key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: Valve disease can cause HF; identify and address valve lesion
key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_MI: Ischemic MR from papillary muscle dysfunction; mechanical complication of MI

sources: Otto CM et al. 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for Valvular Heart Disease. Circulation 2021;143:e72-e227
Vahanian A et al. 2021 ESC Guidelines on Valvular Heart Disease. Eur Heart J 2022;43:561-632

COPD_ASTHMA.definition: COPD exacerbation (AECOPD): acute worsening of respiratory symptoms requiring treatment change. Severe asthma exacerbation: acute/subacute worsening requiring hospitalization. ICU for respiratory failure or impending failure.

vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Tachycardia from hypoxemia, beta-agonists, work of breathing
vital_sign_patterns.spo2: Hypoxemia; TARGET 88-92% in COPD (avoid O2-induced hypercapnia)
vital_sign_patterns.severe_indicators: RR >30, HR >120, SpO2 <90%, accessory muscle use, altered mental status, unable to complete sentences

key_labs.abg_vbg: CRITICAL - pH <7.35 with PaCO2 >45 = respiratory acidosis requiring NIV
key_labs.crp: ≥10 mg/L suggests moderate-severe; helps guide antibiotics

severity_classification.mild: Dyspnea VAS 5-6, RR <24, HR <95, SpO2 ≥92%, CRP <10
severity_classification.moderate: Dyspnea VAS 6-7, RR 24-30, HR 95-110, SpO2 90-92%, CRP ≥10
severity_classification.severe: Dyspnea VAS ≥7, RR >30, HR >110, SpO2 <90%, accessory muscles, AND/OR pH <7.35 with PaCO2 >45

diagnostic_criteria.niv_indications: pH <7.35 and PaCO2 >45; severe dyspnea with accessory muscles; persistent hypoxemia
diagnostic_criteria.intubation_indications: NIV failure, respiratory arrest, inability to protect airway, hemodynamic instability

red_flags: Silent chest in asthma (critical airflow limitation)

key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: Both cause dyspnea, wheezing; HF has elevated BNP, responds to diuretics; COPD responds to bronchodilators
key_differentiators.vs_PNEUMONIA: Pneumonia can trigger AECOPD; fever, focal consolidation, elevated procalcitonin
key_differentiators.vs_PULMONARY_EMBOLISM: Unexplained hypoxia out of proportion → consider PE

sources: GOLD 2023-2026 Reports. www.goldcopd.org
Osadnik CR et al. Cochrane Review: NIV in AECOPD

PANCREATITIS.definition: Acute pancreatitis from premature enzyme activation causing autodigestion. Causes: gallstones (40%), alcohol (40%), hypertriglyceridemia. Severe cases → SIRS, organ failure, necrotizing pancreatitis.

vital_sign_patterns.temperature: Fever indicates SIRS; persistent fever after day 7-10 suggests infected necrosis
vital_sign_patterns.spo2: May drop with ARDS or pleural effusions

severity.mild: No organ failure, no local complications
severity.moderately_severe: Transient organ failure (<48h) OR local complications

diagnostic_criteria.bisap: BUN >25, Impaired mental status, SIRS, Age >60, Pleural effusion. ≥3 = higher mortality (AUC 0.92)
diagnostic_criteria.marshall_score: ≥2 points = organ failure: PaO2/FiO2 <300, Cr >1.9, SBP <90

red_flags: Infected necrosis (fever + deterioration after day 7-10; gas on CT)

key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_MI: Both cause epigastric pain; pancreatitis has lipase ≥3x, no ST changes
key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: Severe pancreatitis mimics sepsis; infected necrosis = true sepsis
key_differentiators.vs_SURGICAL_COMPLICATION: Post-op pancreatitis common after abdominal/cardiac surgery

sources: Banks PA et al. Classification of Acute Pancreatitis (Atlanta 2012). Gut 2013;62:102-111
Tenner S et al. ACG Guidelines: Management of Acute Pancreatitis. Am J Gastroenterol 2013;108:1400-15

COVID.definition: COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2 infection) causing respiratory failure. Characterized by bilateral pneumonia, ARDS, hypercoagulability, and cytokine storm. Biphasic course: viral phase (days 1-7) then inflammatory phase (days 7-14).

vital_sign_patterns.spo2: Silent (happy) hypoxemia - severe hypoxemia with minimal dyspnea initially
vital_sign_patterns.respiratory_rate: May be deceptively normal early despite low SpO2; then rapid deterioration

key_labs.ferritin: >500 indicates inflammation; very high suggests cytokine storm

diagnostic_criteria.diagnosis: PCR or antigen positive for SARS-CoV-2

severity.critical: ARDS, septic shock, or multi-organ failure

key_differentiators.vs_PNEUMONIA: Similar presentation; COVID has bilateral GGO, lymphopenia, silent hypoxemia, biphasic course
key_differentiators.vs_SEPSIS: COVID can cause sepsis picture; distinguish viral vs bacterial
key_differentiators.vs_PULMONARY_EMBOLISM: High VTE risk in COVID; consider if unexplained deterioration

sources: NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines
Ruan Q et al. Clinical Predictors of Mortality in COVID-19. Intensive Care Med 2020

SYNCOPE.definition: Transient loss of consciousness from cerebral hypoperfusion with rapid onset, short duration, and spontaneous complete recovery. ICU for high-risk syncope with suspected cardiac etiology or hemodynamic instability.

vital_sign_patterns.blood_pressure: Hypotension at presentation suggests volume depletion or cardiogenic; orthostatic drop indicates orthostatic etiology
vital_sign_patterns.heart_rate: Bradycardia or tachycardia highly significant; irregular rhythm suggests AF
vital_sign_patterns.note: Vitals often normalized by ICU admission; telemetry captures transient arrhythmias

key_labs.troponin: Elevated suggests ACS; part of Canadian Syncope Risk Score
key_labs.hemoglobin: Anemia (Hct <30%) is risk factor; GI bleed can cause syncope
key_labs.bnp: Elevated suggests HF or structural heart disease

san_francisco_syncope_rule.criteria: CHESS: CHF history, Hct <30%, abnormal ECG, Shortness of breath, SBP <90

canadian_syncope_risk_score.components: Vasovagal predisposition (-1), Heart disease (+1), SBP <90 or >180 (+2), Elevated troponin (+2), Abnormal QRS axis (+1), QTc >480ms (+2), QRS >130ms (+1), ED diagnosis vasovagal (-2), ED diagnosis cardiac (+2)
canadian_syncope_risk_score.interpretation: ≤-1 very low risk (<1%); 0-1 low (<1%); 2-3 medium (5%); 4-5 high (12%); ≥6 very high (>50%)

red_flags: Syncope while supine (rules out vasovagal - implies cardiac)
ECG abnormalities (long QT, Brugada, WPW, AV block)

key_differentiators.vs_STROKE_NEURO: Stroke has persistent focal deficits; syncope has complete recovery
key_differentiators.vs_AFIB_ARRHYTHMIA: AF is common cause; VT is high-risk cause; telemetry essential
key_differentiators.vs_PULMONARY_EMBOLISM: PE presents with syncope in ~10%; consider if hypoxic
key_differentiators.vs_GI_BLEED: GI bleed can present with syncope; check hemoglobin

sources: Quinn JV et al. San Francisco Syncope Rule. Ann Emerg Med 2004
Thiruganasambandamoorthy V et al. Canadian Syncope Risk Score. CMAJ 2016; JAMA Intern Med 2020

PULMONARY_EMBOLISM.definition: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus causing V/Q mismatch, hypoxemia, and RV strain. Massive PE causes hemodynamic collapse; submassive PE causes RV dysfunction without shock.

vital_sign_patterns.spo2: Hypoxemia may be disproportionate to exam

key_labs.d_dimer: High sensitivity for ruling out if low pre-test probability; age-adjusted for >50y
key_labs.troponin: Elevated indicates RV injury; risk stratification
key_labs.lactate: Elevated with hypoperfusion in massive PE

pesi.components: Age, male sex, cancer, HF, chronic lung disease, HR ≥110, SBP <100, RR ≥30, temp <36, AMS, SpO2 <90%
pesi.classes: I-II low risk (1-3.5% mortality); III intermediate (3-7%); IV-V high (4-25%)

diagnostic_criteria.spesi: Age >80, cancer, cardiopulmonary disease, HR ≥110, SBP <100, SpO2 <90%. Score 0 = low risk; ≥1 = high risk

risk_stratification.intermediate_high: sPESI ≥1 + RV dysfunction + elevated troponin → ICU, consider rescue reperfusion
risk_stratification.intermediate_low: sPESI ≥1 with RV dysfunction OR biomarker (not both)
risk_stratification.low_risk: sPESI 0, no RV dysfunction → consider outpatient

key_differentiators.vs_ACUTE_MI: Both cause chest pain, troponin elevation; PE has RV strain, hypoxemia, D-dimer
key_differentiators.vs_HEART_FAILURE: Acute HF can present similarly; echo helps distinguish
key_differentiators.vs_PNEUMONIA: Both cause dyspnea, hypoxemia; PE usually no fever/productive cough

sources: Konstantinides SV et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for Acute PE. Eur Heart J 2020;41:543-603
Aujesky D et al. PESI Derivation and Validation. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2005
